Technical Interpretation

The server_usage.csv trace captures 187,963 machine-level observations across 1,310 production servers over an 11.92-hour window (timestamps 39,600 to 82,500 seconds). Overall data integrity is exceptionally high, with zero duplicate entries and only a single incomplete record (0.00053% missing rate) in the CPU, disk, and load-average fields. Rather than dropping this row globally during preprocessing, all 187,963 records are retained and missing values are filtered at analysis time, yielding 187,962 valid CPU–memory paired observations. Across the cluster, all CPU (0.50%–89.72%) and memory (2.30%–95.42%) measurements fall within valid bounds, and average memory utilization (48.95%) is substantially higher than average CPU utilization (26.47%), indicating potential CPU–memory resource imbalance. Finally, continuity checks against the 300-second baseline interval reveal 669 potential reporting gaps (667 of 600 s and 2 of 1,800 s), which should be considered when interpreting short-term temporal fluctuations.

Source: updated Member B Task 1 summary; row counts, missingness, duplicates and per-machine sampling gaps cross-checked with the uploaded cleaned_server_usage.csv.

QUALITY & PREPARATION

Preserve all observations; filter only for analysis

Updated Task 1 preprocessing policy: all 187,963 input records are retained in cleaned_server_usage.csv. The single partially missing row is not dropped globally. CPU–Memory paired computations use 187,962 valid pairs (pairwise complete observations). No filling, rounding, or fabricated measurements were applied. Each machine's consecutive timestamps were checked against the 300-second baseline, identifying 667 intervals of 600 seconds and two of 1,800 seconds.
01 · Obtain

Use the Alibaba Cluster Trace 2017 source and record the exact dataset version and files.

02 · Inspect

Run 01_dataset_exploration.ipynb to inspect schema, row counts, timestamps, nulls, duplicate rows and basic statistics.

03 · Validate

The original row count is preserved in the normalized file. Missingness is handled by analysis-specific filtering (pairwise complete observations for CPU versus memory).

W1 deliverable: accessible dataset, schema inspection, research questions and data-quality findings. Detailed preprocessing and comparative charts proceed in W2–W3. Source-download and raw-data access are described in the official repository.

Technical interpretation · W1: Mean memory utilization (48.95%) exceeds mean CPU utilization (26.47%) by about 22.48 percentage points in this trace. This motivates investigating CPU–memory mismatches in Task 3; the difference in overall means alone does not prove per-machine resource imbalance, causation or poor application performance.

Member A preprocessing verification

The original input has 187,963 rows. The prepared dataset retains all 187,963 rows, including one row with missing CPU, disk and load-average values. No values were imputed or globally dropped. CPU–memory paired analysis uses the 187,962 rows with both fields present.

Machine-level timestamp checks use the most common 300-second step as the observed baseline. They flag 669 longer intervals (667 × 600 s; 2 × 1,800 s) as potential reporting gaps, not confirmed machine outages. Member A also delivered validation scripts, quality reports and tests.
